findings.resolution: Version 1.1 binds a closed source inventory, toolchain, normalized execution result, package inventory, findings, and sole-maintainer review; every substitution now fails replay.
findings.summary: The first H13 record asserted completion without binding exact executed evidence or accountable review.

findings.resolution: Each inject, expectation, observation, outcome, and complete ordered normative action list is now exact and independently mutation-tested.
findings.summary: The first validator did not independently require every shutdown, quarantine, rotation, verification, advisory, and preservation action.

findings.resolution: Schema validity, evidence validity, and release acceptance are now separate outputs, and the stacked A05/H13 ledger records both completed commits and the correct total.
findings.summary: The first implementation conflated schema validity with acceptance and left the inherited A05 status/count stale.

findings.resolution: The capture command now derives canonical individual test outcomes, command exits, real package inventories, and actual tool versions from executed processes.
findings.summary: The version 1.1 receipt hashed maintainer-declared counts instead of generated command outcomes.

findings.resolution: Capture now hashes every tracked working-tree path and byte with three explicit self-reference exclusions and requires zero other untracked files.
findings.summary: The version 1.1 seven-file source inventory omitted transitive test, build, package, schema, manifest, and documentation inputs.

findings.resolution: Findings now require severity, summary, owner, target milestone/date, lifecycle state, and consistent resolution chronology; valid open findings prevent acceptance.
findings.summary: The version 1.1 finding model could not honestly represent structured open findings and their ownership or due dates.

findings.resolution: Replay compares the current toolchain to the captured versions and explicitly reports current-replay or historical-attestation.
findings.summary: The version 1.1 verifier did not distinguish a matching current runtime from validation of a historical execution.

findings.resolution: Capture now requires identical bounded HEAD, index, tracked, untracked, inventory, and working-byte closures before and after every exercised command, with explicit mutation-during-run tests.
findings.summary: The version 1.2 receipt did not prove that the exercised source remained immutable for the complete command interval.

findings.resolution: The sole-maintainer review-subject digest now covers the receipt and source bindings, every scenario and finding field, the complete review metadata, and the release decision, with capture and resolution chronology enforced.
findings.summary: The version 1.2 review digest covered only the review object and allowed findings, scenarios, or release acceptance to change outside the accountable review subject.

findings.resolution: Every capture and probe subprocess now has explicit time and output bounds, normalized status, signal, timeout, and duration evidence, forced termination, an overall deadline, and finally-block cleanup.
findings.summary: The version 1.2 subprocesses could hang indefinitely and did not bind termination or timeout state.

findings.resolution: Capture validates the declared pnpm@11.18.0 version against a resolved executable identity and binds both pnpm and Node executable digests; unavailable bounded current probes are reported as historical attestation rather than hanging replay.
findings.summary: The version 1.2 runtime probe used an unbounded ambient pnpm lookup without binding its exact execution context.

findings.resolution: Closure collection now bounds Git output, file count, individual and aggregate bytes; sanitizes Git repository/config/index/object environment; rejects hard links; rechecks directory ancestry; and requires the exact four unique package identities.
findings.summary: The version 1.2 closure and package parser lacked complete resource, hard-link, Git-environment, ancestry, and uniqueness controls.

findings.resolution: The asynchronous runner creates an isolated process group, kills the complete descendant tree on timeout, and bounds post-kill cleanup; a real grandchild write-after-timeout test proves containment.
findings.summary: The version 1.3 timeout killed only the direct child and could leave descendants running.

findings.resolution: One monotonic deadline is propagated through Git and test discovery, bounded filesystem reads, executable/source hashing, parsing, commands, post-checks, and bounded temporary cleanup.
findings.summary: The version 1.3 overall deadline did not govern closure, filesystem, hashing, parsing, discovery, and cleanup phases.

findings.resolution: Validation now requires fixed canonical argv, exact accountable hashes for all 24 TUF and 40 non-self standards identities, and exact names and file counts for all four packages, defeating fully rebound forged receipts.
findings.summary: The version 1.3 schema allowed a fresh fully rebound receipt to substitute plausible commands, test identities, and package counts.

findings.resolution: Capture binds pre/post working metadata in addition to bytes and index state; a real child mutates and restores a tracked sentinel during guarded execution and is rejected.
findings.summary: The version 1.3 pre/post byte closure could miss a tracked-file mutation restored before the final snapshot.

findings.resolution: Git, Node, and pnpm resolve only through approved absolute identities, reject symlinks and non-regular files, verify fixed digests through no-follow handles, and recheck identity after execution; Git discovery is NUL-delimited.
findings.summary: The version 1.3 capture still trusted ambient executable resolution and did not couple execution to race-checked approved tool bytes.

findings.resolution: Current capture now runs inside a digest-pinned Docker Linux PID namespace and proves forced removal against a detached, TERM-ignoring, delayed-write, output-overflow adversary.
findings.summary: Process-group cleanup cannot contain a detached session leader, so the prior current-capture acceptance was withdrawn.

findings.resolution: The contained package audit injects exact absolute Node, pnpm, Git, tar, and shell paths from the immutable runtime and rejects prepared dependencies outside that runtime.
findings.summary: The package audit must execute only injected, receipt-bound Node, pnpm, Git, tar, and shell identities.

findings.resolution: Approved host executables are copied through no-follow handles into private single-link files, digest-checked before execution, and rechecked afterward; swap-and-restore tests execute only the sealed bytes.
findings.summary: Approved executable path inspection was not coupled to the exact bytes executed across pathname swaps.

findings.resolution: One monotonic capture deadline now governs bounded source reads and hashes, parsing, contained commands, termination, and awaited forced container and temporary-file cleanup; unavailable containment fails closed.
findings.summary: Filesystem, parsing, hashing, termination, and cleanup must share one hard absolute deadline without background work.

findings.resolution: The explicit preparation step now verifies exact raw OCI index, platform-manifest, and configuration bytes; npm integrity and shasum; every prepared input byte; deterministic rootfs and runtime-overlay archives; and repeated exact OCI manifest, configuration, and layer identities from two FROM-scratch offline builds.
findings.summary: The prior image build did not prove complete base and package-manager provenance or eliminate mutable build-time dependency resolution.

findings.resolution: Every command now uses an explicit private PID namespace request and persists one exact pre-start inspected Config, HostConfig, mount, image, network, resource, and pull-policy configuration plus its canonical digest; mutation tests reject every bound leaf.
findings.summary: The prior receipt did not bind the complete effective container confinement configuration used before command start.

findings.resolution: Container creation now uses CSPRNG names and exact ownership labels, preflights collisions, reconciles timeout, malformed-output, and lost-transport outcomes, revalidates image and ownership before awaited forced removal, and proves zero residual labeled containers under the one deadline.
findings.summary: An unknown container-create outcome could leave an untracked process tree after lost or malformed client results.

scenarios.expected: Acquisition stops; offline scans retain the verified lock and report stale status without claiming freshness.
scenarios.inject: The allowlisted registry is unavailable after the last verified stable activation.
scenarios.observed: The operator selected offline continuation from the prior lock, retained evidence, and did not relax transport or freshness policy.

scenarios.expected: Publication and acquisition stop; the affected online identity is quarantined while immutable evidence is retained.
scenarios.inject: Registry bytes no longer match the signed metadata graph and an online identity may be compromised.
scenarios.observed: The operator stopped both paths, quarantined the affected identity, and preserved signed metadata, logs, versions, and digests.

scenarios.expected: In-band recovery is rejected; a reviewed executable release supplies a new out-of-band root and users receive an advisory.
scenarios.inject: Enough root custodians may be compromised to satisfy the current threshold.
scenarios.observed: The operator rejected downloaded-root recovery, retained evidence, and selected the normal release/provenance path for a new anchor.

scenarios.expected: Rotation uses sequential roots and old/new thresholds, issues fresh online metadata, and resumes only after clean verification.
scenarios.inject: A root-authorized timestamp key reaches its planned rotation date.
scenarios.observed: The operator rotated the key through root continuity, reset hostile fast-forward state, and verified the complete fresh graph before resuming.

scenarios.expected: New threshold-signed metadata withdraws the target; immutable history and an affected-version advisory remain available.
scenarios.inject: A previously published standards target is confirmed harmful for a supported engine range.
scenarios.observed: The operator selected signed withdrawal without deleting history or rewriting user locks and retained the affected digest evidence.

scenarios.expected: Only the original live receipt can roll back immediately; after exit a fresh verified update is required.
scenarios.inject: Post-activation validation fails first in-process and then after the activating process has exited.
scenarios.observed: The operator used no reconstructed authority, preserved committed-state evidence, and selected the correct path for each lifecycle state.

scenarios.expected: Activation is rejected before lock mutation; the compatible lock remains and exact engine guidance is published.
scenarios.inject: The signed candidate requires an engine newer than the running supported version.
scenarios.observed: The operator preserved the compatible state and evidence, rejected metadata editing, and selected compatibility guidance instead.
